name: Common bird's-foot-trefoil
grown_as: A native perennial wild flower of short grassland, lawns and banks; a key food plant for common blue butterflies
habit: Low and sprawling, 10 to 40 cm, many thin solid stems spreading from a woody base, the tips turning up. Mostly hairless.

leaf.type: Compound: five leaflets, three at the tip of a short stalk and two at its base, close to the stem, which look like stipules
leaf.leaflets: All unstalked; the top three spread like a small fan; the lower two often lopsided
leaf.outline: Each leaflet small, oval to obovate, 3 to 10 mm
leaf.stalk: Very short; real stipules are just tiny brown dots

flower.form: Pea flowers held in a ring at the top of a stalk, like a small crown
flower.colour: Bright yellow; buds and the backs of the standards often red or orange-streaked (the 'eggs and bacon' look)
flower.behind: A small calyx, the two upper teeth bent toward each other; a three-part leafy bract under the flower head
flower.carried: 2 to 7 flowers spreading in a ring at the top of a long stalk from the leaf joints, well above the leaves

fruit: Straight, thin, cylindrical pods 1.5 to 3 cm, spreading from the stalk top like the toes of a bird's foot, green turning brown-black and twisting as they split. Seeds tiny, round, brown.
seedling: Two small oval seed leaves, then small three-leaflet leaves before the full five-leaflet leaves
winter: Dies back to a few low, short shoots at the woody base, sometimes reddened

leaf: five small oval leaflets: three at the tip, two down at the base by the stem
bloom: a ring of 2 to 7 yellow pea flowers on a long stalk
red-orange tints on buds or standards
young: a low sprawling mat of thin stems
flower: yellow flower crowns on long stalks
seedhead: spread from the stalk top like a bird's foot
dormant: a few short low shoots at a woody base

look_alikes: Greater bird's-foot-trefoil (Lotus pedunculatus) is taller and hairier with hollow stems and more flowers per head, in damp places. Meadow vetchling has tendrils and only two narrow leaflets. Horseshoe vetch has many pairs of leaflets and wavy, segmented pods. Black medick has tiny yellow balls.
